meaning: to leave hurriedly and in secret, usually to escape arrest or to avoid a debt
sentence: The cashier absconded with three months of collections and was traced only after the bank filed a complaint.

meaning: to state something firmly and publicly; also to uphold a decision made by a lower authority
sentence: The High Court affirmed the tribunal's order, and the pensioners finally received their arrears.

meaning: to make someone feel unfriendly or cut off from a group they once belonged to
sentence: His habit of correcting everyone in public alienated even the colleagues who had once defended him.

meaning: to gather together a large quantity of something over time
sentence: Over forty years the retired schoolmaster amassed a library that filled every wall of the house.

meaning: a short and interesting account of a real incident, usually told to make a point
sentence: She opened the lecture with an anecdote about her first day in the laboratory, and the room relaxed at once.

meaning: confident in a loud and tactless way that others find offensive
sentence: The brash young reporter interrupted the minister twice and was asked to leave the hall.

meaning: to strengthen or give support to an argument or a structure; also a projecting support built against a wall
sentence: He buttressed his case for a new bridge with ten years of accident figures from the old one.

meaning: to plan or devise something with ingenuity; also to manage to do something in spite of difficulty
sentence: With two planks and a length of wire the villagers contrived a stretcher and carried him eight miles.

meaning: deserving blame for something that has gone wrong
sentence: The inquiry found the contractor culpable for using sand in place of cement in the foundation.

meaning: large and awkward to carry or use; also slow and needlessly complicated
sentence: The old registration procedure was so cumbersome that farmers gave up halfway through it.

meaning: not having enough of something that is needed
sentence: The soil here is deficient in nitrogen, which is why the leaves yellow long before the harvest.

meaning: quiet and ready to accept instruction or control without protest
sentence: The mare was docile enough for a beginner, but she shied at the sound of firecrackers.

meaning: to include a wide range of things; also to surround something completely
sentence: The syllabus encompasses everything from ancient trade routes to the economics of the present decade.

meaning: to form a picture in the mind of something expected in the future
sentence: The planners envisage a footbridge here once the second platform is finished.

meaning: to make unfair use of someone for one's own gain, or to use a resource well; also a bold and notable deed
sentence: The mill exploited its weavers for decades, paying them by the piece and charging them for the thread.

meaning: an uneasy feeling that something bad is about to happen
sentence: The unnatural stillness of the sea filled the fishermen with foreboding, and not one boat put out that morning.

meaning: to prevent something by taking action before it can happen
sentence: The municipality forestalled a water riot by announcing the tanker timings a day in advance.

meaning: filled with something undesirable; also tense and full of anxiety
sentence: The last stretch of the descent was fraught with loose scree, and the guide roped the party together.

meaning: to gather information or grain little by little from what others have left
sentence: From half a dozen scattered letters the historian gleaned enough to date the fort to the 1740s.

meaning: to dwell on one's own success or another's misfortune with open satisfaction
sentence: It was a fine win, but gloating over it in the opponents' dressing room cost him the captaincy.

meaning: to seize and struggle with someone in close combat; also to wrestle with a difficult problem
sentence: The committee is still grappling with the question of who should pay for the repairs.

meaning: a feature so distinctive that it identifies its owner or maker; also an official stamp on gold or silver
sentence: Short sentences and a refusal to flatter the reader are the hallmarks of her prose.

meaning: the practice of professing standards or beliefs that one's own conduct does not obey
sentence: There is a certain hypocrisy in lecturing the class on punctuality and then arriving late oneself.

meaning: to dip something wholly into a liquid; also to involve oneself deeply in an activity
sentence: He immersed himself in the archive for six weeks and emerged with a manuscript nobody had expected.

meaning: to reduce someone to poverty; also to drain something of its richness or variety
sentence: Three failed monsoons impoverished a district that had never before asked for relief.

meaning: so firmly fixed by long habit that it is very hard to change
sentence: The habit of checking the rope twice was so ingrained that he did it even on level ground.

meaning: to call on a law, an authority or a name as a reason or a support for what one is doing
sentence: The librarian invoked a rule from 1962 and refused to let the manuscript leave the building.

meaning: to push or knock against people roughly, as in a crowd
sentence: Passengers jostled one another on the narrow platform as the last train of the night pulled in.

meaning: using very few words, sometimes to the point of seeming curt
sentence: His reply to the eight-page complaint was laconic: two lines and a signature.

meaning: a very great and uncountable number of something
sentence: A myriad of small repairs, none of them urgent, had been postponed until the roof finally gave way.

meaning: calmly unconcerned about something that might be expected to worry one
sentence: He was nonchalant about the result, though he had checked the noticeboard four times that morning.

meaning: to destroy something so completely that no trace of it remains; also to blot writing out
sentence: One season of monsoon rain obliterated the inscription that had survived three hundred years.

meaning: so small in amount as to be almost insulting
sentence: A paltry sum was set aside for repairs, and the school roof leaked through another monsoon.

meaning: deeply and rather sadly thoughtful
sentence: She grew pensive at the station, turning the unopened letter over and over in her hands.

meaning: to read something through carefully and at length
sentence: He perused the tenancy agreement line by line before he would put his name anywhere near it.

meaning: to make someone less angry by doing or saying something that pleases them
sentence: A free replacement and a written apology placated the customer who had threatened to go to court.

meaning: to prove a statement or a person to be wrong by producing evidence
sentence: A single photograph of the dam taken that morning refuted the whole of the contractor's account.

meaning: to send someone or something down to a lower rank or a less important place
sentence: After two poor seasons the club was relegated to the second division and lost half its sponsors.

meaning: continuing without any let-up or softening
sentence: The relentless heat of that fortnight emptied the streets between eleven and four.

meaning: official permission or approval for an action; also a penalty imposed to force obedience
sentence: The trustees gave their sanction to the new wing, and building began within the month.

meaning: to examine something closely and critically for faults or detail
sentence: The auditor scrutinised every voucher from March and found two that had been signed twice.

meaning: to suppose something is true from slight evidence rather than from proof
sentence: From the mud on his boots she surmised that he had walked the long way round the lake.

meaning: to interfere with something without permission so as to damage or alter it
sentence: The seal on the ballot box was checked hourly so that nobody could tamper with the votes.

meaning: to push something forward suddenly and with force; also the main point of an argument
sentence: The thrust of her objection was not the cost of the scheme but the speed at which it had been approved.

meaning: to weaken something gradually and often by indirect means
sentence: Constant rumours about the treasurer undermined a trust the society had taken decades to build.

meaning: capable of working successfully; also of a seed or an infant, capable of surviving
sentence: A canteen open only two hours a day was never going to be viable, whatever the fees.

meaning: wanting or devouring great quantities of food; also extremely eager in pursuing something
sentence: He was a voracious reader who finished two novels on the journey down and started a third at the station.

meaning: highly skilled at something through long practice
sentence: She proved adept at calming angry customers within her first week at the counter.

meaning: unselfish concern for the welfare of other people
sentence: His altruism was genuine; he refused to let the new ward carry his name.

meaning: a confusing and difficult problem; or a riddle whose answer turns on a pun
sentence: Feeding a growing city without draining its river is the conundrum every planner meets.

meaning: to involve something as a necessary part or consequence
sentence: Command entails answering for every mistake made by those under you.

meaning: a young bird just learning to fly; or new to an activity and still inexperienced
sentence: The fledgling airline owned two aircraft and flew to a single city.

meaning: an outward appearance put on to conceal the true nature of something
sentence: The old tax was brought back under the guise of a development levy.

meaning: public respect or honour openly shown to someone
sentence: The village pays homage to its first schoolteacher on her birthday every year.

meaning: something that encourages a person to work harder or act in a particular way
sentence: A small monthly bonus proved a better incentive than any number of warnings.

meaning: a particular point in a course of events, usually a critical one; or a place where two things join
sentence: At this juncture the committee had to choose between a long delay and open disgrace.

meaning: slim, supple and able to move with ease
sentence: The gymnast was so lithe that she seemed to have no bones at all.

meaning: a disease or ailment; or a deep-seated problem in a society or system
sentence: Corruption is a malady that no single law has ever managed to cure.

meaning: harmful or poisonous, especially to health
sentence: Noxious fumes from the tannery forced the school to shut for two days.

meaning: a statement or situation that seems to contradict itself and yet may be true
sentence: It is a paradox that the busiest people are often the ones who find time to help.

meaning: the highest point of achievement or success; or a tall pointed turret on a building
sentence: Winning the national title was the pinnacle of a career fifteen years in the building.

meaning: to set right something that is unjust; or compensation given for a wrong
sentence: The villagers went to court to seek redress for the grazing land taken from them.

meaning: to recall past experiences with pleasure and talk about them
sentence: The two old classmates reminisced about the flood that shut the school for a month.

meaning: a brief minor fight away from the main action; or a short sharp argument
sentence: A skirmish at the border was settled by nightfall without a shot being fired.

meaning: not flowing and therefore stale; or showing no growth or activity
sentence: The economy stayed stagnant for three years and the mills closed one after another.

meaning: full of twists and bends; or so long and complicated as to be hard to follow
sentence: The tortuous mountain road added four hours to what should have been a short drive.

meaning: to undo something knitted or tangled; or to investigate something complicated until it is explained
sentence: It took the auditors a year to unravel how the money had left the account.

meaning: a small trace left of something that has otherwise disappeared
sentence: Only a vestige of the old fort survives, a single wall behind the bus stand.
